investigation: Washington paired ZIP-to-tract allocation: scope reconciliation and measured allocation error

exclusion_descriptions.tract_outside_state: the geocoded tract lies outside the state whose crosswalk is under test; the vehicle is registered in-state but garaged or geocoded elsewhere, and the comparison is a within-state one
exclusion_descriptions.unusable_zip_or_tract: the row carries no 5-digit ZIP Code or no 11-digit 2020 census tract, so it cannot enter a paired comparison at all
exclusion_descriptions.zip_below_minimum_ev_count: fewer than 10 observed EVs, so the observed share vector is noise rather than evidence; pre-registered in L1-0 before any result
exclusion_descriptions.zip_no_mapping_hud_res_ratio: method 'hud_res_ratio' returns no tract mapping for this ZIP, so it cannot be scored; reported as unallocatable, not rescued
exclusion_descriptions.zip_no_mapping_land_area: method 'land_area' returns no tract mapping for this ZIP, so it cannot be scored; reported as unallocatable, not rescued
exclusion_descriptions.zip_zero_weight_hud_res_ratio: method 'hud_res_ratio' returns weights summing to zero for this ZIP (no residential addresses). Never renormalised

supersedes: docs/evidence/L1-1_washington_allocation_validation.json, which reported the same comparison but published only the included denominator (292,581) without accounting for the 1,612 excluded records by reason
why_washington: Washington EV registration records carry both a postal ZIP Code and a 2020 census tract on the same observed vehicle row, so the observed ZIP-to-tract EV distribution is directly measurable. This is NOT national ground truth.
